title: Mods Approve Before You're Asked
caption:
Mods can approve a tool call before the prompt ever reaches me.

Claude Code 2.1.287 turned them on by default on October 1. Nothing runs until I install a plugin that contains one, but the moment I do, that code sits inside Claude Code with my permissions: my files, my env vars, my API key, every prompt I send. Not sandboxed. Turn sandboxing on and it guards the Bash commands Claude runs, not a process the mod starts.

The admission: I installed three plugins last month and read none of them. claude plugin validate lists every event a mod handles and every call it makes, without running a line of it. I had never run it once.

Which mods are you running?

Mods Approve

slides.sub: Claude Code 2.1.287, October 1. Mods are on by default: JavaScript that runs inside Claude Code, with your permissions.

slides.headline:
Mods Aren’t
Sandboxed
slides.sub: Turn sandboxing on and it isolates the Bash commands Claude runs. A process a mod starts runs outside it.

slides.title: What A Mod Reaches
items: Your files and processes, as you. Env vars and settings files, including an API key.
Every prompt you send and every tool call Claude makes. It can rewrite them.
A call an ask rule would prompt for, or one your own PreToolUse hook blocked.
